decisions.reason: The digital anamnesis and consent app is a flagship line that builds directly on the firm's core knowledge of dental practice workflows and data integration, so the firm can interpret its results and keep improving it.

The education institute draws on the firm's practitioner-informed training content and close customer relationships, and it helps users absorb new features and regulations, although it lies somewhat outside the software core.
Remote screen-sharing support is a low-cost extension of the firm's established customer support capability, and remote work after 2020 likely made it more valuable.
The analytics dashboard uses the practice data the firm's software already holds and its existing engineering knowledge, which fits the direction toward efficiently managed digital practices.
The complete practice bundle repackages modules the firm knows well for new practices, but bundles are often reshaped or renamed, which gives a moderate risk of withdrawal.

The job and practice listing portal is furthest from the firm's software and support knowledge and was only mentioned on the website, so its value is hard to assess, but its low running costs and its role in building community with the customer base argue for keeping it for now.
